31	func newResumeCmd() *cobra.Command {
32		var force bool
33	
34		cmd := &cobra.Command{
35			Use:   "resume [branch]",
36			Short: "Resume a stopped session (interactive picker, or by branch)",
37			Long: `Resume an agent session.
38	
39	With no argument, opens an interactive picker of stopped sessions across all
40	worktrees so you don't have to remember which branch you left work on. Picking
41	a session checks out its branch and shows the command to continue the agent. If
42	the branch is already checked out in another worktree, you'll be pointed there
43	instead.
44	
45	With a branch argument, switches to that branch and resumes its session directly:
46	1. Checks out the specified branch
47	2. Finds the session ID from commits unique to this branch (not on main)
48	3. Restores the session log if it doesn't exist locally (an existing local log
49	   is kept as-is; use --force to overwrite it from the checkpoint)
50	4. Shows the command to resume the session
51	
52	If the branch doesn't exist locally but exists on origin, you'll be prompted
53	to fetch it.
54	
55	If newer commits without checkpoints exist on the branch (e.g., after merging main
56	or cherry-picking from elsewhere), this operation will reset your Git status to the
57	most recent commit with a checkpoint.  You'll be prompted to confirm resuming in this case.`,
58			Args: cobra.MaximumNArgs(1),
59			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
60				if checkDisabledGuard(cmd.Context(), cmd.OutOrStdout()) {
61					return nil
62				}
63	
64				// Discover external agents so checkpoints from external agents can be resolved.
65				external.DiscoverAndRegister(cmd.Context())
66	
67				if len(args) == 0 {
68					return runResumePicker(cmd.Context(), cmd, force)
69				}
70	
71				return runResume(cmd.Context(), cmd, args[0], force)
72			},
73		}
74	
75		cmd.Flags().BoolVarP(&force, "force", "f", false, "Resume from older checkpoint without confirmation")
76	
77		return cmd
78	}

80	func runResume(ctx context.Context, cmd *cobra.Command, branchName string, force bool) error {
81		// Only initialize logging when inside a git worktree to avoid
82		// creating .entire/logs/ in arbitrary directories.
83		if _, err := paths.WorktreeRoot(ctx); err == nil {
84			logging.SetLogLevelGetter(GetLogLevel)
85			if err := logging.Init(ctx, ""); err == nil {
86				defer logging.Close()
87			}
88		}
89	
90		w := cmd.OutOrStdout()
91		errW := cmd.ErrOrStderr()
92	
93		proceed, err := switchToBranchForResume(ctx, w, errW, branchName, force)
94		if err != nil || !proceed {
95			return err
96		}
97	
98		return resumeFromCurrentBranch(ctx, w, errW, branchName, force)
99	}
100	
101	// switchToBranchForResume ensures the working tree is on branchName, checking it
102	// out (or fetching it from origin) as needed. It returns proceed=false with a nil
103	// error when the user declined to fetch a remote-only branch, so callers should
104	// stop without treating that as a failure.
105	func switchToBranchForResume(ctx context.Context, w, errW io.Writer, branchName string, force bool) (bool, error) {
106		// Check if we're already on this branch
107		currentBranch, err := GetCurrentBranch(ctx)
108		if err == nil && currentBranch == branchName {
109			return true, nil
110		}
111	
112		// Check if branch exists locally
113		exists, err := BranchExistsLocally(ctx, branchName)
114		if err != nil {
115			return false, fmt.Errorf("failed to check branch: %w", err)
116		}
117	
118		if !exists {
119			// Branch doesn't exist locally, check if it exists on remote
120			remoteExists, err := BranchExistsOnRemote(ctx, branchName)
121			if err != nil {
122				return false, fmt.Errorf("failed to check remote branch: %w", err)
123			}
124	
125			if !remoteExists {
126				return false, fmt.Errorf("branch '%s' not found locally or on origin", branchName)
127			}
128	
129			// Ask user if they want to fetch from remote (--force skips the prompt)
130			if !force {
131				shouldFetch, err := promptFetchFromRemote(branchName)
132				if err != nil {
133					return false, err
134				}
135				if !shouldFetch {
136					return false, nil
137				}
138			}
139	
140			// Fetch and checkout the remote branch
141			fmt.Fprintf(w, "Fetching branch '%s' from origin...\n", branchName)
142			if err := FetchAndCheckoutRemoteBranch(ctx, branchName); err != nil {
143				fmt.Fprintf(errW, "Error: failed to checkout branch: %v\n", err)
144				return false, NewSilentError(errors.New("failed to checkout branch"))
145			}
146			fmt.Fprintf(w, "✓ Switched to branch %s\n", branchName)
147			return true, nil
148		}
149	
150		// Branch exists locally, check for uncommitted changes before checkout
151		hasChanges, err := HasUncommittedChanges(ctx)
152		if err != nil {
153			return false, fmt.Errorf("failed to check for uncommitted changes: %w", err)
154		}
155		if hasChanges {
156			return false, errors.New("you have uncommitted changes. Please commit or stash them first")
157		}
158	
159		// Checkout the branch
160		if err := CheckoutBranch(ctx, branchName); err != nil {
161			fmt.Fprintf(errW, "Error: failed to checkout branch: %v\n", err)
162			return false, NewSilentError(errors.New("failed to checkout branch"))
163		}
164		fmt.Fprintf(w, "✓ Switched to branch %s\n", branchName)
165		return true, nil
166	}

168	// resumeSessionOnBranch switches to branchName and resumes the specific session
169	// identified by checkpointID, instead of re-deriving the latest checkpoint on the
170	// branch. The interactive picker uses this so that selecting one of several
171	// sessions on the same branch resumes exactly that session.
172	func resumeSessionOnBranch(ctx context.Context, cmd *cobra.Command, branchName string, checkpointID id.CheckpointID, force bool) error {
173		if _, err := paths.WorktreeRoot(ctx); err == nil {
174			logging.SetLogLevelGetter(GetLogLevel)
175			if err := logging.Init(ctx, ""); err == nil {
176				defer logging.Close()
177			}
178		}
179	
180		w := cmd.OutOrStdout()
181		errW := cmd.ErrOrStderr()
182	
183		proceed, err := switchToBranchForResume(ctx, w, errW, branchName, force)
184		if err != nil || !proceed {
185			return err
186		}
187	
188		return resumeByCheckpointID(ctx, w, errW, checkpointID, force)
189	}
190	
191	// resumeByCheckpointID restores the session(s) recorded in a specific committed
192	// checkpoint and prints the resume command(s). Unlike resumeFromCurrentBranch it
193	// does not search branch history — the caller already knows which checkpoint to
194	// resume, so two sessions on the same branch resume independently.
195	func resumeByCheckpointID(ctx context.Context, w, errW io.Writer, checkpointID id.CheckpointID, force bool) error {
196		if checkpointID.IsEmpty() {
197			return errors.New("no checkpoint to resume")
198		}
199	
200		repo, err := openRepository(ctx)
201		if err != nil {
202			return fmt.Errorf("not a git repository: %w", err)
203		}
204		defer repo.Close()
205	
206		stores, err := checkpoint.Open(ctx, repo, checkpoint.OpenOptions{BlobFetcher: FetchBlobsByHash})
207		if err != nil {
208			return fmt.Errorf("open checkpoint store: %w", err)
209		}
210		store := stores.Persistent
211		refs := stores.Refs()
212		if refs.ReadBootstrappableFromOrigin() {
213			promoteRemoteTrackingPrimary(ctx, repo, refs)
214		}
215	
216		metadata, err := readCheckpointInfoFromStore(ctx, store, checkpointID)
217		if err != nil {
218			if checkpointpolicy.IsUnsupportedVersion(err) {
219				return err
220			}
221			logging.Debug(ctx, "resume by checkpoint: metadata read failed, checking remote",
222				slog.String("checkpoint_id", checkpointID.String()),
223				slog.String("error", err.Error()),
224			)
225			return checkRemoteMetadata(ctx, w, errW, checkpointID, stores.Refs())
226		}
227	
228		return resumeSession(ctx, w, errW, metadata, force)
229	}

233	
234		repo, err := openRepository(ctx)
235		if err != nil {
236			return fmt.Errorf("not a git repository: %w", err)
237		}
238		defer repo.Close()
239	
240		// Find a commit with an Entire-Checkpoint trailer, looking at branch-only commits
241		result, err := findBranchCheckpoints(repo, branchName)

243			return err
244		}

254			slog.Bool("newer_commits_exist", result.newerCommitsExist),
255		)

257		// If there are newer commits without checkpoints, ask for confirmation.
258		// Merge commits (e.g., from merging main) don't count as "work" and are skipped silently.

262			fmt.Fprintf(w, "Checkpoint from: %s %s\n\n", result.commitHash[:7], firstLine(result.commitMessage))
263	
264			shouldResume, err := promptResumeFromOlderCheckpoint()
265			if err != nil {
266				return err
267			}
268			if !shouldResume {
269				fmt.Fprintf(w, "Resume cancelled.\n")
270				return nil
271			}
272		}
273	
274		checkpointID := result.checkpointIDs[0]
275		var metadata *strategy.CheckpointInfo
276	
277		stores, err := checkpoint.Open(ctx, repo, checkpoint.OpenOptions{BlobFetcher: FetchBlobsByHash})
278		if err != nil {
279			return fmt.Errorf("open checkpoint store: %w", err)
280		}
281		store := stores.Persistent
282	
283		refs := stores.Refs()
284		if refs.ReadBootstrappableFromOrigin() {
285			promoteRemoteTrackingPrimary(ctx, repo, refs)
286		}
287	
288		// Multiple checkpoints (squash merge): resolve latest by CreatedAt timestamp.
289		if len(result.checkpointIDs) > 1 {
290			latestMetadata, found, err := resolveLatestCheckpoint(ctx, store, result.checkpointIDs)
291			if err != nil {
292				return err
293			}
294			if !found {
295				// No metadata available — nothing to resume from
296				logging.Warn(logCtx, "no checkpoint metadata resolved",
297					slog.Int("checkpoint_count", len(result.checkpointIDs)),
298				)
299				fmt.Fprintf(w, "Found %d checkpoints for commit %s but metadata is not available\n",
300					len(result.checkpointIDs), result.commitHash[:7])
301				return checkRemoteMetadata(ctx, w, errW, result.checkpointIDs[0], stores.Refs())
302			}
303			olderSkipped := len(result.checkpointIDs) - 1
304			fmt.Fprintf(w, "Found %d checkpoints for commit %s, resuming from the latest checkpoint (%d older checkpoint(s) skipped)\n",
305				len(result.checkpointIDs), result.commitHash[:7], olderSkipped)
306			checkpointID = latestMetadata.CheckpointID
307			metadata = latestMetadata
308		}
309	
310		if metadata == nil {
311			storeInfo, storeErr := readCheckpointInfoFromStore(ctx, store, checkpointID)
312			if storeErr == nil {
313				metadata = storeInfo
314			} else {
315				if checkpointpolicy.IsUnsupportedVersion(storeErr) {
316					return storeErr
317				}
318				logging.Debug(ctx, "checkpoint store metadata read failed",
319					slog.String("checkpoint_id", checkpointID.String()),
320					slog.String("error", storeErr.Error()),
321				)
322				logging.Warn(logCtx, "checkpoint metadata read failed, checking remote",
323					slog.String("checkpoint_id", checkpointID.String()),
324					slog.String("error", storeErr.Error()),
325				)
326				return checkRemoteMetadata(ctx, w, errW, checkpointID, stores.Refs())
327			}
328		}
329	
330		logging.Debug(logCtx, "checkpoint metadata read successfully",
331			slog.String("checkpoint_id", checkpointID.String()),
332			slog.String("session_id", metadata.SessionID),
333			slog.Int("session_count", metadata.SessionCount),
334		)
335	
336		return resumeSession(ctx, w, errW, metadata, force)
337	}

339	// resolveLatestCheckpoint reads metadata for each checkpoint ID and returns the
340	// checkpoint with the latest CreatedAt.
341	func resolveLatestCheckpoint(ctx context.Context, store checkpointInfoReader, checkpointIDs []id.CheckpointID) (*strategy.CheckpointInfo, bool, error) {
342		infoMap := make(map[id.CheckpointID]strategy.CheckpointInfo, len(checkpointIDs))
343		for _, cpID := range checkpointIDs {
344			metadata, readErr := readCheckpointInfoFromStore(ctx, store, cpID)
345			if readErr != nil {
346				logging.Debug(ctx, "resolveLatestCheckpoint: checkpoint metadata read failed",
347					slog.String("checkpoint_id", cpID.String()),
348					slog.String("error", readErr.Error()),
349				)
350				return nil, false, readErr
351			}
352			infoMap[cpID] = *metadata
353		}
354		latest, found := strategy.ResolveLatestCheckpointFromMap(checkpointIDs, infoMap)
355		if !found {
356			return nil, false, nil
357		}
358		return &latest, true, nil
359	}

361	type checkpointInfoReader interface {
362		checkpoint.CheckpointReader
363		ReadSessionMetadata(ctx context.Context, checkpointID id.CheckpointID, sessionIndex int) (*checkpoint.Metadata, error)
364	}

366	func readCheckpointInfoFromStore(ctx context.Context, store checkpointInfoReader, checkpointID id.CheckpointID) (*strategy.CheckpointInfo, error) {
367		summary, err := checkpoint.ReadCheckpoint(ctx, store, checkpointID)
368		if err != nil {
369			return nil, fmt.Errorf("read checkpoint: %w", err)
370		}
371		if err := checkpointpolicy.EnsureCanReadVersion(checkpointID.String(), summary.CheckpointVersion); err != nil {
372			return nil, err
373		}
374		info := &strategy.CheckpointInfo{
375			CheckpointID:     checkpointID,
376			CheckpointsCount: summary.CheckpointsCount,
377			FilesTouched:     summary.FilesTouched,
378			SessionCount:     len(summary.Sessions),
379		}
380		for i := range summary.Sessions {
381			metadata, metaErr := store.ReadSessionMetadata(ctx, checkpointID, i)
382			if metaErr != nil {
383				logging.Debug(ctx, "read checkpoint metadata: session metadata read failed",
384					slog.String("checkpoint_id", checkpointID.String()),
385					slog.Int("session_index", i),
386					slog.String("error", metaErr.Error()),
387				)
388				continue
389			}
390			info.SessionIDs = append(info.SessionIDs, metadata.SessionID)
391			if metadata.SessionID != "" {
392				info.SessionID = metadata.SessionID
393				info.CreatedAt = metadata.CreatedAt
394				info.Agent = metadata.Agent
395				info.IsTask = metadata.IsTask
396				info.ToolUseID = metadata.ToolUseID
397			}
398		}
399		if info.SessionID == "" {
400			return nil, checkpoint.ErrCheckpointNotFound
401		}
402		return info, nil
403	}

405	func readCheckpointInfoFromRef(
406		ctx context.Context,
407		repo *git.Repository,
408		refs checkpoint.PersistentRefs,
409		checkpointID id.CheckpointID,
410	) (*strategy.CheckpointInfo, error) {
411		stores, err := checkpoint.Open(ctx, repo, checkpoint.OpenOptions{Refs: &refs, BlobFetcher: FetchBlobsByHash})
412		if err != nil {
413			return nil, fmt.Errorf("open checkpoint store: %w", err)
414		}
415		return readCheckpointInfoFromStore(ctx, stores.Persistent, checkpointID)
416	}

418	// getMetadataTree returns the metadata branch tree and a fresh repo handle.
419	// After a fetch, go-git's storer cache may be stale (new packfiles on disk
420	// are invisible to the repo opened before the fetch). To avoid this, each
421	// attempt opens a fresh repo after the fetch succeeds.
422	//
423	// Fallback order: treeless fetch → local → checkpoint_remote → full origin fetch → remote tree.
424	func getMetadataTree(ctx context.Context) (*object.Tree, *git.Repository, error) {
425		logCtx := logging.WithComponent(ctx, "resume.getMetadataTree")
426	
427		refs := checkpoint.ResolveRefs(ctx)
428	
429		// Helper to log ref hash for a repo's primary metadata ref
430		logRefHash := func(repo *git.Repository, source string) {
431			ref, refErr := repo.Reference(refs.Primary, true)
432			if refErr != nil {
433				logging.Debug(logCtx, "primary metadata ref not found",
434					slog.String("source", source),
435					slog.String("error", refErr.Error()),
436				)
437				return
438			}
439			logging.Debug(logCtx, "primary metadata ref resolved",
440				slog.String("source", source),
441				slog.String("ref_hash", ref.Hash().String()),
442			)
443		}
444	
445		// When checkpoint_remote is configured, try it first — that's where
446		// checkpoint data lives. Avoids a wasted fetch from origin (which may
447		// not have the metadata branch at all).
448		if fetchErr := FetchMetadataFromCheckpointRemote(ctx); fetchErr == nil {
449			freshRepo, freshErr := openRepository(ctx)
450			if freshErr == nil {
451				logRefHash(freshRepo, "checkpoint-remote")
452				metadataTree, treeErr := strategy.GetMetadataRefTree(freshRepo, refs.Primary)
453				if treeErr == nil {
454					logging.Debug(logCtx, "metadata tree obtained via checkpoint remote fetch",
455						slog.String("tree_hash", metadataTree.Hash.String()),
456					)
457					return metadataTree, freshRepo, nil
458				}
459				logging.Debug(logCtx, "checkpoint remote fetch succeeded but tree read failed",
460					slog.String("error", treeErr.Error()),
461				)
462				_ = freshRepo.Close()
463			}
464		} else {
465			logging.Debug(logCtx, "checkpoint remote fetch skipped or failed",
466				slog.String("error", fetchErr.Error()),
467			)
468		}
469	
470		// Tip-only fetch (--depth=1) is cheap and always runs so the local lookup
471		// below doesn't return stale data.
472		if fetchErr := FetchMetadataTreeOnly(ctx); fetchErr == nil {
473			freshRepo, repoErr := openRepository(ctx)
474			if repoErr == nil {
475				logRefHash(freshRepo, "treeless-fetch")
476				metadataTree, treeErr := strategy.GetMetadataRefTree(freshRepo, refs.Primary)
477				if treeErr == nil {
478					logging.Debug(logCtx, "metadata tree obtained via treeless fetch",
479						slog.String("tree_hash", metadataTree.Hash.String()),
480					)
481					return metadataTree, freshRepo, nil
482				}
483				logging.Debug(logCtx, "treeless fetch succeeded but tree read failed",
484					slog.String("error", treeErr.Error()),
485				)
486				_ = freshRepo.Close()
487			}
488		} else {
489			logging.Debug(logCtx, "treeless fetch failed, trying local",
490				slog.String("error", fetchErr.Error()),
491			)
492		}
493	
494		// Try local (may have been set by a prior fetch or push)
495		localRepo, repoErr := openRepository(ctx)
496		if repoErr == nil {
497			logRefHash(localRepo, "local")
498			metadataTree, err := strategy.GetMetadataRefTree(localRepo, refs.Primary)
499			if err == nil {
500				logging.Debug(logCtx, "metadata tree obtained from local branch",
501					slog.String("tree_hash", metadataTree.Hash.String()),
502				)
503				return metadataTree, localRepo, nil
504			}
505			logging.Debug(logCtx, "local metadata branch not available",
506				slog.String("error", err.Error()),
507			)
508			_ = localRepo.Close()
509		}
510	
511		// Fallback: full fetch from origin
512		if fetchErr := FetchMetadataBranch(ctx); fetchErr == nil {
513			freshRepo, repoErr := openRepository(ctx)
514			if repoErr == nil {
515				logRefHash(freshRepo, "full-fetch")
516				metadataTree, treeErr := strategy.GetMetadataRefTree(freshRepo, refs.Primary)
517				if treeErr == nil {
518					logging.Debug(logCtx, "metadata tree obtained via full fetch",
519						slog.String("tree_hash", metadataTree.Hash.String()),
520					)
521					return metadataTree, freshRepo, nil
522				}
523				logging.Debug(logCtx, "full fetch succeeded but tree read failed",
524					slog.String("error", treeErr.Error()),
525				)
526				_ = freshRepo.Close()
527			}
528		} else {
529			logging.Debug(logCtx, "full fetch failed",
530				slog.String("error", fetchErr.Error()),
531			)
532		}
533	
534		// Try remote tree directly (origin's tracking ref for Primary)
535		remoteRepo, repoErr := openRepository(ctx)
536		if repoErr != nil {
537			return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to open repository: %w", repoErr)
538		}
539		logRefHash(remoteRepo, "remote-tracking")
540		remoteTree, remoteErr := strategy.GetRemotePrimaryTree(ctx, remoteRepo)
541		if remoteErr == nil {
542			logging.Debug(logCtx, "metadata tree obtained from remote-tracking branch")
543			return remoteTree, remoteRepo, nil
544		}
545		logging.Debug(logCtx, "remote metadata tree also not available",
546			slog.String("error", remoteErr.Error()),
547		)
548		_ = remoteRepo.Close()
549	
550		return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("metadata branch not available: %w", remoteErr)
551	}

553	// branchCheckpointsResult contains the result of searching for checkpoints on a branch.
554	type branchCheckpointsResult struct {
555		checkpointIDs     []id.CheckpointID
556		commitHash        string

I've traced the whole flow. Here's what's going on and how I'd fix it.

## Root cause

The bug is in `RestoreLogsOnly` at `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_rewind.go:670-677`:

```go
skipExisting := map[string]bool{}
if !force {
    for _, sess := range s.classifySessionsForRestore(...) {
        if sess.Status != StatusNew {
            skipExisting[sess.SessionID] = true
        }
    }
}
```

`classifySessionsForRestore` already computes a *four-way* status by comparing the local log's last timestamp against the checkpoint's (`ClassifyTimestamps`, line 924):

- `StatusNew` — no local file
- `StatusUnchanged` — same
- `StatusCheckpointNewer` — **the checkpoint has entries the local log doesn't**
- `StatusLocalNewer` — local has entries the checkpoint doesn't (real conflict)

But the skip logic collapses all of `Unchanged` / `CheckpointNewer` / `LocalNewer` into "skip". So the one case that *should* refresh the local log — `StatusCheckpointNewer` — is silently skipped. That's exactly your scenario: machine A pushed an advanced checkpoint (no new code commit, just updated `entire/checkpoints/v1`), machine B already has the older restored log on disk, so resume sees "file exists, not New → skip" and keeps the stale transcript. `claude -r` then opens the old state.

All green. Done. Here's a summary of what I implemented (A + C).

## The bug
`entire resume` (without `--force`) skipped restoring **any** session whose local log already existed — including the case where the checkpoint had *newer* entries than the local copy. So after you pushed an advanced checkpoint from machine A, machine B kept its stale local log and `claude -r` opened the old state.

## The fix
The skip decision now uses the four-way timestamp classification that was already computed but collapsed into a binary "exists → skip":

- **`StatusNew`** (no local file) → restore
- **`StatusUnchanged`** → keep local (no-op)
- **`StatusCheckpointNewer`** → **restore** (A) — the checkpoint is a strict superset, nothing local is lost. Prints `Checkpoint has newer entries than the local log; updating it.`
- **`StatusLocalNewer`** → **prompt before overwriting** (C) — wires up the previously-dead `PromptOverwriteNewerLogs`. Keeps the local log on decline, and in non-interactive mode keeps it with a `use --force` hint rather than erroring.

`--force` still overwrites unconditionally.

## Files changed
- `strategy/manual_commit_rewind.go` — extracted the per-session decision into `decideRestoreActions` (keeps `RestoreLogsOnly` under the complexity limit), added the checkpoint-newer notice in the write loop, and exported `ConfirmOverwriteNewerLocalLogs` (interactive prompt / non-interactive keep).
- `resume.go` — `resumeSingleSession` (the legacy single-session fallback) gets the same timestamp-aware logic instead of a bare `os.Stat`.
- Tests: new `TestRestoreLogsOnly_OverwritesWhenCheckpointNewer`, `TestResumeSingleSession_OverwritesWhenCheckpointNewer`, and rewrote the integration test that previously asserted the buggy behavior (`...KeptEvenWhenCheckpointNewer` → `...RefreshedWhenCheckpointNewer`).
- `CLAUDE.md` — updated the resume behavior description.

Every real resume entrypoint (`entire resume`, `session resume`, the interactive picker, the remote-metadata fallback) funnels through these two functions, so they're all covered. Per your call, `trail` needed no change — `trail checkout` only switches branches and doesn't restore session logs.

Codex found a genuine correctness gap (not a quality nit) — the "Option D" robustness concern we deferred when you chose A+C. My assessment after digging in:

**The finding is valid but the obvious fix has a real downside.** The risk window is narrow — it needs two machines to *independently* continue the **same** session ID and diverge, with the remote one having a newer last-timestamp (sequential "continue on A, resume on B" is fine). The intuitive fix is a line-prefix check: auto-overwrite only when the local log is a clean prefix of the checkpoint, otherwise prompt. **But** the pre-push OPF re-redaction rewrites earlier checkpoint bytes — so a clean continuation could fail a byte/line-prefix check and trigger a *false* "divergence" prompt on exactly the smooth cross-machine flow that feature A was meant to make seamless. That's why timestamps were used originally.

So this is a genuine safety-vs-friction tradeoff that's yours to make:
